text: Kalila, you would never open your mouth up in the sky, right? But 1 flying tortoise did, and almost lost everything!
A flying tortoise? Tortoises can't fly!
This one did, with two kind ducks, and one little stick. Listen!
Once upon a time, by a little green pond, there lived a tortoise and two ducks. They were the best of friends.
The tortoise was kind, but he loved to talk. He talked all day long!
Good morning, ducks! Did you see the sun? Did you see that bee? Did you see my new flower? Did you...
Yes, yes, dear friend. We saw everything!
But one summer, the sun was very hot, and no rain came. Day by day, the little pond dried up.
Oh no! Our pond is almost gone!
We must fly to the big blue lake, far away, over the hills.
Fly? But I cannot fly! Please don't leave me here alone!
We will never leave you, friend. Let us think.
I have an idea! We will hold a stick, one end each. You bite the middle, and hold on tight!
But remember: do not open your mouth. Not one word, until we land!
Not one word? Easy! I promise! I will be as quiet as a stone!
So the tortoise bit the stick. The ducks flapped their wings, and up, up, up they flew!
The tortoise saw the trees, the hills, and the clouds. Oh, how he wanted to talk! But he kept his mouth shut.
Then they flew over a little village. The children looked up, and they pointed and laughed.
Look! Look! Two ducks are carrying a tortoise!
Ha ha! What a silly tortoise!
The tortoise got very cross. Silly? Me? He wanted to answer so much!
Mm! Mm-mm!
I am not silly! I am...
Oh no! He opened his mouth, and he let go of the stick! Down, down, down fell the tortoise...
...right into a big, soft pile of hay! Flump!
Friend! Friend! Are you all right?
I'm all right. My shell is strong. But, oh, I should have kept my mouth shut.
Next time, friend: think first, then speak!
So the three friends walked the rest of the way together, slowly, slowly, all the way to the big blue lake.
Mm-hmm! Mm-hmm!
And this time, the tortoise thought very carefully before every word.
So the tortoise could fly, but he could not wait. One word too early, and down he went!
Think before you speak! Your words can wait a little.
Persian word of the day! In Persian, a tortoise is laak-posht. Laak-posht! It means, a shell on the back!
Laak-posht. A tortoise. And a strong laak saved our little friend today.
And next time: three fish in a pond, and only one of them makes a plan.
